mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AppendOnlyAuditEntries allows Alloy to place two ApplicationEvents with the same (application, eventType) pair, directly violating the append-only invariant. The injection forces exactly such a duplicate into existence, making both AppendOnly and FR_016_AuditTrailComplete find a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj e1, e2: ApplicationEvent | e1.application = e2.application and e1.eventType = e2.eventType }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_OnePendingPerCustomer allows a customer to hold two PendingReview applications simultaneously, violating FR-005. The injection forces two distinct PendingReview applications with the same customer, producing a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_TwoPendingViolation { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.customer = a2.customer and a1.status = PendingReview and a2.status = PendingReview }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_DecisionImmutability allows two Decision rows to reference the same LoanApplication, violating the at-most-one-decision invariant central to FR-011 and FR-012. The injection forces two decisions on the same application.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DoubleDecisionViolation { some disj d1, d2: Decision | d1.application = d2.application }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_PermissionMatrix removes the closed-world assignment of PermMatrix.Allowed, so Alloy can freely assign any (Role, OperationKind) pair as allowed. The injection explicitly grants Customer the PostDecision operation, breaking LeastPrivilege and FR_015.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionMatrixViolation { Customer -> PostDecision in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AttributionDecisionEvents allows a Customer-role user to be the actor on an EvtApproved or EvtRejected event. The injection forces exactly that misattribution, making AttributionCorrectness find a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MisattributionViolation { some e: ApplicationEvent | (e.eventType = EvtApproved or e.eventType = EvtRejected) and e.actor.role = Customer }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_NotificationOnDecision allows an approved or rejected application to exist with no corresponding NotificationLog entry. The injection forces an approved application that has no notification record, making FR_014_NotificationOnDecision find a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingNotificationViolation { some a: LoanApplication | a.status = StatusApproved and (no n: NotificationLog | n.application = a) }
